name: Data Converter
description: Convert anything in one DBX workbench panel: 13 formats (JSON / YAML / XML / Properties / TOML / INI / .env / CSV / TSV / Query / Headers / Cookie / HTML) in any combination, JSONPath / jq queries with JSON Schema validation, eight escape tools (URL / Base64 / HTML / JSON / Unicode / Hex / SQL / Regex), batch text to SQL (IN / NOT IN / INSERT), .xlsx / .csv / .tsv to JSON, Image ⇄ Base64, and a Byte Converter (B/KB/MB/GB/TB/PB on both the 1000 and 1024 scales, exact ⇄ human readable, batch totals, plus hex dump / byte array / binary string). A Code Gen page turns a JSON sample or a CREATE TABLE into TypeScript / Go / Java / Python models, and a Chart page renders an ECharts option (or bare numbers) as a real chart, 700 x 400 by default with custom width and height, exported as PNG or SVG. Pure frontend, no backend, works offline.
releaseNotes:
Every page can now import a file — the page you are on handles it, and the size limit is shown on the drop overlay before you release. The Chart page also digs charts out of real backend exports: a task list whose payload is itself serialized JSON, business keys six layers deep with thousands of table rows in between. Charts that used to be missed are now listed in a Chart picker by title, and the status line says so when an input is too large to scan completely.
0.1.6 (update): a new Chart page renders an ECharts option — or just an array of numbers — as a real chart, 700 x 400 by default with an editable width and height, exported as PNG at 1x / 2x / 3x or as vector SVG; the ECharts 6.1.0 engine ships inside the package, loads only when you open the page and works inside the DBX sandbox. The Image ⇄ Base64 page gained file import, so everything it exports can be imported back. Every save now reports what actually happened (saved, downloaded, cancelled or failed) instead of always claiming success. All ten pages are translated into 14 languages, and everything runs locally: no network, no eval.
